result.title: Can Loan Processors and Underwriters Spot AI-Edited Statements? An Empirical Study
result.summary: AI-assisted editing can produce loan documents that preserve familiar issuer layouts while changing the applicant's identity. We investigated whether experienced underwriters and loan processors identify such forgeries in first-pass, document-only review. Three practitioners recruited through Upwork each received one applicant package drawn from 134 forged PDFs derived from 47 genuine financial documents supplied with full consent. The edits preserved amounts, dates and balances; identifier inconsistencies introduced by the pipeline were knowingly retained before distribution. Reviewers were not told that files had been altered and returned 132 file-level judgements. Checking their explanations against the originals yielded 14 edit-supported concerns (10.6%): 12 Suspicious judgements and two Insufficient information judgements. All supported concerns involved identifier disagreements within or across documents, and no reported visual cue identified an actual edit. Thus, approximately one in ten judgements contained evidence of the forgery, despite known inconsistencies remaining in the files. These observations motivate evaluating consistency checks and independent source verification alongside human review. With three reviewer-package pairs and no genuine-file controls, the findings describe this exploratory setting rather than population-wide detection accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文让三名贷款审核从业者在仅看文件的初轮审查中判断 AI 篡改过的贷款申请材料，并统计其判断中有多少能由真实编辑痕迹支持，结果约一成判断获得证据支持。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是关于人类审查员识别文档伪造的小样本实证研究，不涉及 VLM 内部表示、latent 推理状态、证据获取或训练监督，也未提出可供迁移的计算方法线索，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
